# 子夏易傳

## Authors / Editors
- 卜商 (周朝) 撰 -507 - -400

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A commentary in 11 *juàn* on the *Zhōuyì* 周易 ([KR1a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0001)), traditionally ascribed to [卜商](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8D%9C%E5%95%86) Bǔ Shāng (Zǐxià), one of [孔丘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E4%B8%98) Confucius's senior disciples. The received text is a layered pseudepigraph: not a Hàn-era survival, but a Táng-period fabrication associated with [張弧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%BC%A7) Zhāng Hú, further altered after the Southern Sòng. The Sìkù 四庫 editors retained it in the canon only as a textual specimen. The frontmatter dating window (618–1279, Táng through Southern Sòng) reflects the assumed actual composition and recompilation history of the received recension, not the lifedates of the attributed author.

**Abstract**

The work is attributed to Bǔ Shāng (Zǐxià), a senior disciple of Confucius. There is no contemporary or early-Hàn evidence that the historical Zǐxià composed a *Yì* commentary: the *Hànshū Yìwénzhì* 漢書藝文志 lists no such work, and [劉向](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%90%91) Liú Xiàng's *Qīlüè* (extant only in fragments and quotations) is the earliest source even to mention one. A six-*juàn* *Zǐxià Yì* first appears as a discrete catalogue entry in [阮孝緒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%AD%9D%E7%B7%92) Ruǎn Xiàoxù's *Qīlù* (Liáng dynasty); the *Suíshū Jīngjí zhì* notes that even this had shrunk from six *juàn* to two by its time, and that the attribution drifted between Zǐxià, [韓嬰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E5%AC%B0) Hán Yīng, and [丁寬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%81%E5%AF%AC) Dīng Kuān. The Tang state already regarded the text as problematic enough to commission editorial work in 719 CE.

The received eleven-*juàn* recension descends from a separate Táng fabrication associated with [張弧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%BC%A7) Zhāng Hú (a *píngshì* 評事 in the Dàlǐsì), as [晁說之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%81%E8%AA%AA%E4%B9%8B) Cháo Yuèzhī first argued and as the Sòng *Guóshǐ zhì* and *Chóngwén zǒngmù* effectively confirm by listing genuine and spurious *Zǐxià Yì* in parallel. [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) Zhū Yízūn's *Jīngyì kǎo* showed that even this Táng text was further altered after the Southern Sòng: passages cited as *Zǐxià* by [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng, [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò, and [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) Wáng Yīnglín are absent from the present text, so the received recension is not even Zhāng Hú's intact. Internal evidence supports the picture: the chapter division follows [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì's arrangement, an arrangement that postdates the historical Zǐxià by some seven centuries. [馬國翰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E5%9C%8B%E7%BF%B0) Mǎ Guóhàn's *Yùhán shānfáng jíyì shū* 玉函山房輯佚書 (Qīng) reconstructs a separate two-*juàn* fragmentary text from these earlier citations, conventionally treated as the closest available witness to whatever pre-Táng *Zǐxià Yì* tradition existed.

The eleven-*juàn* text printed in the *Sìkù quánshū* (Wényuāngé edition, V7.1, p1) is the version preserved in the catalogue as a "specimen of one school" (姑存以備一家); the editorial *tiyao* of 1780, signed by [紀昀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B4%80%E6%98%80) Jǐ Yún and his colleagues, sets out the case for layered pseudepigraphy at length and remains the locus classicus for the textual problem.
